mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has oscillated in a narrow band (-25.7 to -27.6) over the last four weeks without a clear trend break, indicating inertia in retail footfall recovery. This momentum persists absent a new shock, keeping the next four weeks' mean close to the last four weeks' mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC ranged -25.7 to -27.6 over the last 4 weeks with no clear directional break
failure_condition: If mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds the last-28-day mean by more than 2 points, the momentum/inertia claim is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has declined steadily for four straight weeks (-17.4 to -24.1), suggesting households are curbing outdoor discretionary trips, likely due to heightened caution or weather. This reduced outdoor activity propensity should spill over into reduced discretionary retail visits over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls more than 3 points week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from -17.4 to -24.1 over four weeks, accelerating in the most recent week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC mean over the next 2 weeks rises relative to the last 2 weeks despite PARKS continuing to decline, the spillover mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES have both stabilized in the most recent two weeks (TRANSIT ~-30, WORKPLACES ~-20.4), indicating a settled commuting pattern. When both series plateau simultaneously, retail visits tied to commute routes (e.g., station-adjacent retail) stabilize as well, producing a flat-to-slightly-positive RETAIL_REC trend over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT held near -29.7 to -30.4 and WORKPLACES near -20.4 to -20.7 over the last two weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC continues to decline over the next 4 weeks even though both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain flat (within 1 point), the joint-stabilization mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-July marks the typical end of Japan's rainy season (tsuyu) in the Tokyo region, after which outdoor and shopping activity historically rebounds as weather improves. This seasonal transition should lift RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks independent of policy or infection dynamics.
evidence_refs: fact:decision date 2020-07-15 falls near the typical end of Tokyo's rainy season
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC and PARKS both continue to decline or remain flat over the next 2 weeks despite seasonal improvement, the seasonal-rebound hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The Go To Travel domestic stimulus campaign was slated to launch in Japan in mid-to-late July 2020, intended to boost consumer spending and travel-related retail activity. If implemented as planned, this policy stimulus should raise RETAIL_REC over the following four weeks by encouraging discretionary outings.
candidate_trigger: national travel/consumption stimulus program takes effect
evidence_refs: fact:decision date 2020-07-15 precedes planned national stimulus policy rollout
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC fails to rise or declines further over the next 4 weeks despite the stimulus policy being in effect, the policy-stimulus mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has moved toward baseline (from -5.0 to -3.7, with a dip to -2.4), signaling a partial normalization of essential shopping behavior. When essential-shopping normalization outpaces discretionary retail recovery, it suggests households are prioritizing essential trips while limiting broader retail visits, which should suppress RETAIL_REC over the next week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM improves by more than 2 points over two weeks while RETAIL_REC stays flat or worsens
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -5.0 to -3.7 over four weeks while RETAIL_REC stayed flat near -27
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises in the next week alongside continued GROCERY_PHARM improvement, the essential-vs-discretionary substitution hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has remained persistently elevated (10.9-11.1) for four weeks, indicating sustained work-from-home and reduced overall outbound trip generation. This structural constraint on outbound mobility caps any meaningful recovery in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed between 10.9 and 11.1 over the last four weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises by more than 2 points over the next 4 weeks while RESIDENTIAL stays at or above 10.9, the capping hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Tokyo experienced a resurgence in reported COVID-19 cases in early-to-mid July 2020, plausibly prompting renewed informal caution even without formal lockdown. The concurrent acceleration of PARKS decline alongside flat TRANSIT suggests early behavioral tightening that should translate into falling RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks if case counts keep rising.
candidate_trigger: PARKS declines more than 3 points week-on-week while TRANSIT remains flat or worsens
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS dropped 3 points in the most recent week while TRANSIT stayed near -30.4
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rises over the next 2 weeks even as PARKS continues to decline and TRANSIT stays flat, the renewed-caution mechanism is rejected.
